Subject: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & cost levers (recap + next steps)

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciated the visibility into the Nova Retail chat use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can size a short benchmark and give a cost estimate.

Recap of requirements you mentioned:
- Target latency: p95 <= 200ms for 1:1 chat response end-to-end (streaming preferred)
- Throughput: steady-state ~120k responses/month, peak ~600 reqs/min (burst)
- Concurrency: typical 20-30 concurrent users, peak ~80 concurrent sessions
- Streaming: token-by-token streaming required for conversational UI (low perceived latency)
- Quality: equivalent to ~13B open models; can trade model size vs quantization if quality maintained
- Budget sensitivity: prefer hosted/shared unless cost forces dedicated capacity

Cost/perf levers we discussed (high level):
- Continuous batching (shapes latency/throughput tradeoffs)
- KV/prefix caching for repeated prompts (saves compute for common queries)
- Quantization profiles (int8 / awq) to reduce GPU memory & cost (potential quality impact)
- Model variants: smaller quantized variant for interactive paths, larger model for heavyweight calls (rerank/long-generation)
- Streaming chunk size tuning (smaller chunks reduce time-to-first-byte but increase token compute overhead)

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll share our SLO playbook (attached) and a short perf checklist.
2) Could you send 1-2 representative payloads (single-turn and multi-turn) + an estimate of average token distribution? Please put in the attached filenames or reply here.
3) We’ll run a 30-min perf run at target concurrency (we usually do 10/30/80 concurrency profiles) and return: p50/p95 latencies, throughput, and cost estimate across configs (hosted vs dedicated, quantized vs fp16).

Attached: redwood-performance-slo-playbook.pdf (performance checklist + suggested configs).

If that sounds good I’ll loop in Rishi (inference lead) and Priyom (solutions) to scope the benchmark and timeline.

Thanks,

—Marissa Cole

Alex —

Perfect — thanks for the color. We’ll run the benchmark and report the following metrics:
- Latency: p50, p90, p95 (end-to-end request/response) and time-to-first-token (streaming)
- Throughput: requests/sec and tokens/sec at each concurrency profile
- GPU metrics: utilization, memory footprint, and effective batch sizes
- Cost: estimated $/1k responses and monthly run-rate for the observed profile (hosted fp16, hosted int8, dedicated int8)

Recommended initial config for the benchmark (what we’ll test):
1) Model variants:
   - 13B fp16 (baseline quality)
   - 13B int8 quantized (recommended first pass for cost savings)
   - 7B int8 fast path for routing small assistant responses (lower cost)
2) Batch policy: continuous batching with target batch size 48-64 tokens (we’ll tune based on payloads)
3) Caching: prefix/KV caching for the top ~10% of repeated queries (we’ll need sample prompts to identify)
4) Streaming: small chunk size (~16-32 token chunks) to hit perceived latency SLO while keeping overhead low
5) Fallback routing: route large/long-generation requests to a larger model instance (or dedicated slot) to avoid degrading interactive latency

Operational recommendations (short):
- Start hosted with quantized 13B to validate quality; if sustained growth, evaluate Dedicated reservations for better unit economics.
- Use workload-aware batching rules for interactive vs backend (rerank) paths to avoid tail latency spikes.

- Rishi/Priyom to scope the benchmark (expected 2-3 days of runs) and schedule a 30-60 min sync to review results.
